branches.title: When does video 3D consistency predict downstream failure?
branches.stage: literature conflict: metric novelty blocked; pivot under audit
branches.question: Do geometry-specific failures in generated video predict downstream task errors after matching perceptual quality and camera motion?
branches.novelty: MEt3R (CVPR 2025) compares multi-view consistency; PDI-Bench (2026) already measures object rigidity and motion in generated video; PAIWorld (2026) studies robotic multi-view geometry. A generic rigidity metric alone is NOT a new contribution. Seek a causal downstream link or a falsifiable limitation of existing scores.
branches.pilot: Use an existing geometry-labeled benchmark or render 20 rigid scenes. Apply controlled object deformation at fixed camera trajectory and quality, then test whether PDI/MEt3R scores and a simple planner change in a monotone way. No video generator training.
branches.stop: Stop if the effect is already established by prior downstream planning studies, or if planner failure cannot be attributed to geometry rather than realism.

PDI-Bench: Quantitative Video World Model Evaluation for Geometric-Consistency

branches.title: Mask selection as a side channel
branches.stage: informed-missingness prior art found; SSL-specific novelty unproven; no GPU required
branches.question: Does an adaptive mask reveal information about hidden tokens, even when the predictor never sees those tokens?
branches.novelty: A mask pattern can encode properties of hidden content: 'informative missingness' was already studied by GRU-D (Che et al., Scientific Reports 2018). Teacher/student-guided adaptive masking is also established, e.g. AAAI 2025 CMT-MAE. Thus generic 'mask indices leak label information' is NOT novel. Possible narrower question: does content-conditioned mask selection leak reconstruction information beyond visible patches and thereby inflate MIM pretraining metrics? An actual MIM control is required.
branches.pilot: Use a balanced toy target Y and mask M, show that 10% mask-bit flip noise yields 1-H2(0.1)=0.531 bits of information (algebraic sanity check only); then audit one public masked-image model with fixed visible-token count, teacher-based vs independent masks, mask-only, visible-only, visible+mask and label-permuted mask probes. Estimate I(Y;M | visible tokens) with held-out estimates. Match token count, mask histogram, and compute. Zero GPU for toy; modest inference for checkpoint.
branches.stop: If held-out conditional leakage is negligible once spatial count and visible information are matched, or existing SSL work already studies identical diagnostics, retire the leak claim; consider negative-result methodology instead.

branches.title: Interpretability of layer positions and feature routing
branches.question: Do particular attention heads or layer locations carry causal semantic information beyond easy probe correlations?
branches.novelty: Prior work already finds OCR heads with a verbalization lens; cannot repeat that claim.
branches.pilot: Replicate one released causal intervention on a small vision-language model; compare target-head ablation, layer-matched random heads and input controls.
branches.stop: If effects vanish against layer-matched controls, record a negative result.

branches.title: Entity linking recall under fixed candidate cost
branches.question: Can uncertainty-aware retrieval increase complete-link recall without inflating candidate lists?
branches.novelty: Blocking, multi-view retrieval and multilingual embeddings are mature; must show novel cost/recall trade-off.
branches.pilot: Use a frozen untouched stratified holdout; compare exact blocks, char n-grams, transliteration, adaptive caps and reverse retrieval at identical average candidate budget.
branches.stop: If pair recall improves but complete-link recall and cost do not, downgrade.

branches.title: Budget-matched pretraining data selection
branches.question: Can cheap data selection beat uniform sampling at the same tokens, wall-clock time, and selection overhead?
branches.novelty: Compare to strong recent data-mixture and data-selection baselines, not only uniform.
branches.pilot: Run small-model repeated seeds on fixed corpora, report selection compute plus training compute and held-out perplexity.
branches.stop: If total-cost gains disappear, pivot to an analysis of where selection fails.

branches.title: Do temporal boundaries help downstream memory?
branches.question: Can detected event boundaries improve temporal retrieval or question answering at equal frame budget?
branches.novelty: Boundary F1 alone cannot establish downstream usefulness.
branches.pilot: Compare ground-truth boundaries, predicted boundaries, uniform frames and random frames with the same total frames and fixed downstream model.
branches.stop: If gains disappear under matched budget or on untouched videos, stop.

branches.title: Structured conditions versus captions in action recognition
branches.question: When does verifying discrete temporal conditions outperform a descriptive video caption?
branches.novelty: Simple action benchmarks may make both approaches similar; avoid dataset-specific claims.
branches.pilot: Select temporal minimal-pair actions; fix the video encoder and reasoner, match inference tokens, compare condition-based and caption-based evidence.
branches.stop: If both are tied on hard temporal shifts, refocus on calibration/failure analysis.

branches.title: Agent-made experiments that survive audit
branches.stage: execution-vs-correctness overlap found; test harness defined
branches.question: Can a constrained research agent make real improvements under withheld tests and a counted human-intervention budget?
branches.novelty: CausalVerify (Sep 2026) already shows that executing end-to-end AI-written scientific workflows does not establish numerical correctness. Autoresearch already automates bounded model training. A new 'agents can write and execute papers' result is NOT novel. Distinct possible result: audit adaptive experiment selection under a frozen wall-clock budget using held-out seeds and independent replication.
branches.pilot: One public small-model autoresearch task and a fixed baseline; hold out three pre-registered seeds never used for edit selection. Record every attempted edit, failed run, wall-clock and compute budget, selected winner on development split, and unbiased held-out performance. Compare best-of-N selected updates with fixed random-search updates and an untouched human baseline. This is a protocol only; no runs have occurred.
branches.stop: If full accounting removes the apparent improvement or a published agent-audit benchmark already tests the same selection-bias protocol, pivot to a reproducibility report rather than a novelty claim.

closestPriorArt.title: CausalVerify: end-to-end execution is not correctness (Sep 2026)

branches.title: Audio-event segmentation at matched compute
branches.question: Can a simple constrained decoder improve boundaries without a larger speech model?
branches.novelty: Event segmentation already has many decoders; inspect benchmark leakage and timing conventions.
branches.pilot: Compare fixed thresholds, median filtering, dynamic programming and uncertainty-aware decoders on held-out recordings.
branches.stop: If improvement is limited to one dataset or noisy labels, do not claim a general method.

branches.title: Causal study of generated-video geometry errors in robot planning
branches.stage: high prior-art overlap; only action-ranking-regret question retained; pilot gate
branches.question: For a fixed robot planner and task, which kinds and severity of generated-video geometry faults actually change plan feasibility, rather than only visual similarity?
branches.novelty: What-If World (2026) already benchmarks paired physical interventions in generated driving/manipulation videos, but explicitly leaves downstream utility unmeasured. CausalNav (Aug 2026) reports that structural world-model fidelity need not predict control benefit. ExecutionBridge (Oct 2026) studies a frozen planner under controller-induced execution shift. A general 'causal videos for planning' claim is NOT novel. Candidate: isolate exactly when rigid-object 3D geometry errors flip a frozen planner's action ranking, with matched visual corruption and oracle state controls.
branches.pilot: Start with a reproducible 2D tabletop/grid setup: 2 obstacle configurations × 3 distortion strengths × 3 independent seeds (18 paired scenarios), fixed initial scene, camera, goals, planner, scoring and proposals. Geometric edits must not alter task truth. Compare action-ranking flips, collisions, margin to next-best action, PDI/MEt3R-type score, and appearance-matched non-geometric corruptions. Positive evidence must replicate on withheld scenes before any 3D claims. This is a PROPOSED design; zero runs.
branches.stop: If 2026 prior work already tests geometry-specific action-ranking regret under frozen policies, or distortion effects disappear after matching appearance and oracle state, retire/pivot. No RSS abstract without a genuinely distinct mechanism and controlled pilot.

closestPriorArt.title: What-If World: causal benchmark without tested downstream utility (2026)
CausalNav: model fidelity versus control benefit (Aug 2026)
Plans Are Not Executions: frozen planners and execution shift (Oct 2026)

branches.title: Small formal proofs for retrieval and selection
branches.question: Which simple assumptions guarantee a recall-cost bound for multi-route retrieval or adaptive sampling?
branches.novelty: A theorem needs nontrivial assumptions, an actual proof and numerical checks.
branches.pilot: State a two-route probabilistic model; derive a bound; brute-force check small instances and construct counterexamples.
branches.stop: If bound is vacuous under realistic distributions, retire.

branches.title: Transfer of synthetic-image evaluation to biology
branches.question: Do geometry metrics fail in predictable ways on microscopic synthetic sequences with no real paired view?
branches.novelty: Biomedical evaluation needs meaningful validated controls, not clinical claims.
branches.pilot: Use public synthetic cell-like renderings with controllable deformations and illumination; compare geometric and perceptual consistency metrics.
branches.stop: If results do not transfer beyond toy images, retain as a methods note only.

branches.title: Are networked research experiments truly reproducible?
branches.question: How often do agent-driven optimization claims vanish under controlled placement, contention and seed variance?
branches.novelty: A benchmark alone needs a novel reproducibility protocol or generalizable systems finding.
branches.pilot: Run small synthetic services with controlled load and resource contention; measure throughput, latency and variance before/after each agent change.
branches.stop: If differences are explainable by noise, don't claim an optimization.

policies.rule: Generative AI may be used only for grammatical correction; disclosure is required.
Entirely AI-written or AI-developed papers will be desk rejected.
Entirely AI-generated papers and thinly sliced submissions risk desk rejection or sanctions.
Mandatory manuscript AI-use disclosure; authors are responsible for all claims and originality.
LLM use permitted; disclosure encouraged, reproducibility and correct citations mandatory.

LLM assistance is permitted with human responsibility. A mandatory LLM Usage Statement must disclose tools, stages, and extent, including grammar editing. Without an eligible reciprocal reviewer among coauthors, an author may appear on at most one submission; overall 25-paper author cap. OpenReview profiles and author lists must be ready by Nov 10.

Substantive LLM-generated technical content must be disclosed; editing, literature search, and code assistance alone do not require disclosure. Eight main-track submissions maximum per author; no placeholder abstract; potential ACM open-access APC.
